latest.title:
The Future of Cloud Computing
Give me the paragraph, discription,
latest.description: The future of cloud computing is expected to be more advanced, intelligent, and secure. Technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), the Internet of Things (IoT), and edge computing are making cloud services more powerful. Businesses can use cloud platforms to store large amounts of data, develop applications, and improve their services.

latest.title: Your AWS Application Is Running. But Is It Actually Healthy?
latest.description: An application can be running and still have problems. Learn how AWS monitoring helps detect errors, performance issues, and failures.

latest.title: When 40% Give Up Before Hello World: Why I Built an AI Twin for AWS Student Builders
latest.description: How I built StudentPathOS, an AI companion that cuts AWS student onboarding from 3 hours to 15 minutes with live verification, portal comparisons, and milestone celebrations.

latest.title: I Built Fuuud AI, a Gentle Agent That Helps You Find the Right Care
latest.description: Fuuud AI is an agent built on Amazon Bedrock that helps people find the right doctor, hospital, or pharmacy, and knows when to point someone to emergency help instead of chatting.

latest.title: "Please hold": teaching a phone agent to wait politely while it searches
latest.description: When our voice agent searched its knowledge base, callers heard seconds of silence and talked over it. Here is how we added hold music, kept every word the caller said during the search, and checked every change against real calls with per-call telemetry in Amazon S3.

latest.title: Build an Agent Weekend Challenge: Billsense
latest.description: An AWS bill-explainer agent that tells you whether to worry first, then why, with a Panic Meter, plain-English answers and charts from Cost Explorer data.

latest.title: Weekend Challenge: Untangle
latest.description: A sixty second ramble goes in. One sentence you actually said comes back, along with the thing you were avoiding saying. Here is how I built it on Lambda, Transcribe and Bedrock in a weekend, and the one design decision that made people stop treating it like a chatbot.

latest.title: 5 IAM Mistakes I Made Giving an AI Agent Access to My AWS Account
latest.description: Giving an AI agent access to your AWS account feels like a shortcut until its permissions get out of hand. This article covers five IAM mistakes that turn a helpful assistant into a security risk, and how to fix each one. You will learn to build least-privilege action groups, scope each role to a single job, and use short-lived credentials. You will also see what happens when a poisoned input tricks an over-permissioned agent into acting for an attacker. Copy-ready policy examples are included for each fix.

latest.title: From Learner to Builder: My Journey into AWS Cloud Computing
latest.description: Starting with cloud computing can feel overwhelming, but learning one concept at a time makes it easier. Discover how beginners can learn AWS, build hands-on projects, explore cloud services, and grow their skills through consistent practice and community learning.

latest.title: Building a Generative AI Chatbot with Amazon Bedrock, Claude 3 Haiku, LangChain, and Streamlit
latest.description: Learn how to build and deploy a Streamlit chatbot using Amazon Bedrock and Claude 3 Haiku on AWS EC2. This hands-on guide covers environment setup, IAM permissions, Python dependencies, deployment steps, troubleshooting, and making your AI chatbot accessible through a web browser.

trending.title: Strands Box on AWS Lambda MicroVMs: a kernel per agent, a policy per command, and a fleet to run them with microvm-ctl
trending.description: Strands Box checks every shell command, file and request an agent makes against a Dogwood policy. Lambda MicroVMs give the agent its own kernel. I built Box for aarch64 Linux, ran it inside Lambda MicroVMs, and drove fleets with microvm-ctl: 83 ms per box, 22.7 boxes/s per 1 GB VM, 64 of 64 correct across 8 VMs, a playground app, and the bugs I hit.

trending.title: AWS MCP Server... Now in 6 New Regions
trending.description: The AWS MCP Server is now available in six more AWS Regions... Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Ireland, London, and Oregon. If you're using AWS in one of those regions, and working with AI coding assistants (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, etc), this is for you. Read more... 👇

trending.title: A Physical AI Robot Episode Judge That Knows When It Does Not Know: Strands Decider in Strands Robots
trending.description: I added Strands Decider as an opt-in episode-judge backend in strands-labs/robots. It labels a recorded robot episode with one HTTP request (about 1.8 s), returns calibrated probabilities, and writes a label only when it is confident. On a 12-episode MuJoCo test it wrote zero wrong labels and left every unsure episode, with its probabilities, for the existing VLM judge.

trending.title: Introducing Events on AWS Builder Center
trending.description: Starting today, builders can find and register for events hosted by AWS Heroes, Community Builders, User Group Leaders, and Student Builder Group Leaders on Builder Center, and get reminders and updates as push notifications in the AWS Builder app.

trending.title: La Gran Mentira de los Contenedores: Por Qué un Contenedor Docker NO Es una Máquina Virtual Ligera
trending.description: Si has trabajado en desarrollo de software o infraestructura en los últimos cinco años, probablemente has escuchado la analogía clásica para explicar Docker: "Un contenedor es simplemente como una máquina virtual, pero más ligera y rápida".

trending.title: How I Trained the Best 2B Strands Decider: Beating the Official Strands Model and the 2B Leaders, Top 3 in Text, Image and Multimodal
trending.description: I unlocked image input in Strands Decider, then trained four 2B-class checkpoints that beat the published v19 and, by my estimate, take the top 3 spots on the 2B text board, #2 on images and the best text+image slot. This is the full engineering story: the benchmark rules, a 27B yes/no teacher, a base-model bake-off, a calibration fix, a text+image model that broke and was repaired, and an unseen-task check against the 2B leaders. All scores are local and unofficial.

trending.title: AWS Lambda Response Streaming for Kotlin and Java
trending.description: Implementing HTTP response streaming behind API Gateway without writing a custom JVM runtime or adding Lambda layers.

trending.title: Introducing feature-level notifications with API and CloudFormation filters on Capabilities by Region in AWS Builder Center
trending.description: Starting today, builders can get notified about a single feature in any AWS Region, including future ones, and filter 19,000+ API operations and 5,000+ AWS CloudFormation resource types down to the differences between Regions.

trending.title: A Token Without a Name: Bedrock Cost Attribution
trending.description: How we trace every Amazon Bedrock token to a user, team and feature with CUR 2.0 IAM principal data, invocation logs and Amazon Managed Grafana.

trending.title: Pour one out for Infrastructure Composer
trending.description: A personal farewell to Infrastructure Composer, the Stackery journey behind it, and the people who made it matter.
